addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- trello-skill: Use when the user asks to create, manage, or query Trello boards, lists, cards, labels, members, checklists, or comments
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

# Roadmap operativa

Task in ordine approssimativo. Ogni voce è abbastanza grossa da meritare
una sessione di lavoro dedicata, abbastanza piccola da chiudersi
indicativamente in 1-2 giorni. Niente fasi formali, niente stime, niente
date — l'ordine si aggiusta in base agli attriti che emergono in corsa.

La fonte di verità su architettura, decisioni e razionale resta
[riepilogo-design.md](./riepilogo-design.md). Questo file è solo l'elenco
operativo dei task con il loro stato.

## Tracer bullet — la prima cosa che gira end-to-end

- [x] **1. Setup dual-repo dev.** Cartelle siblings `digital-hub/` (il
  package core) e `atmosphera-hub/` (il template cliente), path repo
  Composer nel `composer.json` del template, multi-root workspace VSCode
  (`atmosphera-stack.code-workspace`).
  - Deviazione dal design: le cartelle non si chiamano `core/`/`template/`
    ma `digital-hub/`/`atmosphera-hub/`. Il package è
    `atrioteam/digital-hub` (namespace `AtrioTeam\DigitalHub\`),
    service provider `DigitalHubServiceProvider`.

- [x] **2. Package `core` (`digital-hub`) skeleton.** `composer.json` con
  dipendenze, PSR-4 autoload, `DigitalHubServiceProvider` con
  register/boot funzionanti.
  - Versioni risolte: `laravel/framework ^13.0`, `filament/filament ^5.0`,
    `filament/minimal-theme ^5.0.0-beta4`,
    `bezhansalleh/filament-shield ^4.2`, `spatie/laravel-permission ^7.4`,
    `spatie/laravel-medialibrary ^11.22`, `spatie/laravel-activitylog ^5.0`,
    `kalnoy/nestedset ^7.0`, `spatie/laravel-health ^1.39`.
  - Deviazione dal design: aggiunta `filament/minimal-theme` (fork
    `atrioteam/filament-minimal-theme-fork` via VCS repo) + tema custom
    (`resources/theme/digital-hub-theme.css` + `.scss`) applicati dal
    `DigitalHubPlugin`. Il design non menzionava un tema.
  - Tutti i SP auto-discovered in `bootstrap/cache/packages.php` di
    atmosphera-hub (transitivi via path repo).

- [x] **3. Skeleton template Laravel (`atmosphera-hub`).** Laravel fresh +
  Filament v5 install + admin panel base (`AdminPanelProvider` registra
  `DigitalHubPlugin`), `require atrioteam/digital-hub: @dev` via path repo,
  `.env`, DB.
  - Deviazione dal design: il template richiede anche
    `spatie/laravel-translatable ^6.14` (per i `name` localizzati, vedi
    sezione "Decisioni emerse") e dipende dal package
    `atrioteam/filament-helper` (working dir separata) per
    `TranslationSection`/`SeoFields`/auto-traduzione DeepL.

- [ ] **4. Auth + ruoli + super-admin.** `User` model con trait
  `HasRoles`, `Gate::before()` super-admin in `AuthServiceProvider`,
  `RoleSeeder` con `super-admin`/`Admin`/`Editor`/`Viewer`,
  `php artisan shield:generate` per i permessi iniziali.

- [x] **5. Trait `HasTechnicalAttributes` nel core.** API
  `attr/setAttr/attrLabel/attrOption`, locale-aware reads, query scopes
  `whereAttr`/`whereAttrBetween`, colonna configurabile via
  `$attributesColumn`, static + dynamic schema resolution.
  - Deviazione dal design: il trait NON dichiara le static properties
    `$attributesColumn`/`$attributeSchemaClass` per evitare il PHP
    property compatibility check tra trait e classe usante. I modelli
    le dichiarano direttamente, il trait le legge via `property_exists()`.

- [x] **6. `AttributeSchema` base + `Type` DSL nel core.** Classe
  astratta con `attributes()` e `groups()`. `Type` fluent:
  string/int/decimal/bool/date/enum/text con modificatori
  required/min/max/regex/in/unit/translatable/filterable. Validation
  che applica le rule sul save.

- [x] **7. `AttributesEditor` Filament component nel core.**
  `for(Model::class)` che legge lo schema, genera gli input giusti,
  raggruppa con `Tabs`, reattivo via Livewire.
  - Reattività (re-render sul cambio di `ProductType`) rimandata al task #17.
    Oggi l'editor è risolto staticamente alla prima render del form.

- [x] **8. `Product` + `ProductAttributes` + `ProductResource` nel
  template.** Migration con colonna `attributes` JSON, schema con 2-3
  attributi (es. `sku` string, `weight` decimal, `wood_type` enum),
  resource minimale (name, slug, `AttributesEditor`).
  - **Schema attributi del Product**: due ruoli distinti.
    - `ProductAttributes` → schema **generico/default** (`sku`, `weight`,
      `wood_type`), agganciato dal `ProductTypeSeeder` alla tipologia
      "Generico". È lo schema di base per i prodotti senza tipologia
      specifica.
    - `Divani` (e future `Lampade`, `Tavoli`, …) → schemi **per-tipologia**,
      con gli attributi dipendenti dalla `ProductType`. Oggi `Divani` è
      vuota: si popolerà quando ci saranno attributi reali specifici della
      tipologia, nell'ambito della composizione PHP (task #17, design §3.4/3.5).
  - `Product` usa `HasGlobalId` + `HasTechnicalAttributes` +
    `HasTranslations` (name localizzato). Vedi "Decisioni emerse".

- [x] **9. Gerarchia catalogo (Category1 + Category2 + ProductType) nel
  template.** Tre entità Eloquent separate al posto del singolo `Category`
  + nested-set originariamente previsto. La gerarchia è fissata in codice
  (numero di livelli noto a priori per cliente), niente strutture
  flessibili runtime-configurabili.
  - **Category1** (Categoria) → `HasMany Category2`. Label cliente:
    "Categoria"/"Categorie". Schema attributi `Category1Attributes` (vuoto
    inizialmente, applicabile via `HasTechnicalAttributes`).
  - **Category2** (Collezione) → `BelongsTo Category1`, `HasMany Product`.
    Label cliente: "Collezione"/"Collezioni". Schema attributi
    `Category2Attributes`.
  - **ProductType** (Tipologia prodotto) → entità autonoma cross-categoria,
    contiene il campo `attribute_schema_class` (FQN della schema class).
    Label cliente: "Tipologia prodotto"/"Tipologie prodotto". Seedata con
    una tipologia default "Generico" che punta a `App\Pim\Schemas\ProductAttributes`.
  - **Product** → `BelongsTo Category2` + `BelongsTo ProductType`. Lo
    schema attributi è risolto dinamicamente da
    `productType->attribute_schema_class` (override di
    `resolveAttributeSchemaClass()` nel modello). Lo static
    `$attributeSchemaClass` non è più dichiarato sul Product.
  - **Naming convention**: classi `Category1`/`Category2` generiche;
    tabelle `categories_1`/`categories_2` (sovrascritte via
    `$table`); file traduzioni `lang/{locale}/category1.php`,
    `category2.php`, `product_type.php` (matcha `Str::snake(class_basename())`).
    Il refinement del trait è stato applicato per supportare i nomi
    composti (es. `ProductType` → `product_type`).
  - **Drill-down navigation**: click sulla riga + azione esplicita "Figli"
    (Collezioni / Prodotti) sulla colonna actions; breadcrumb
    ricostruisce la catena Categorie → Collezione → Prodotti.
  - **Niente nested-set** in catalogo. `kalnoy/nestedset` resta installato
    nel core ma non usato qui — disponibile per eventuali alberi
    utente-driven futuri (es. menù navigazione).
  - **Niente "famiglia" come concetto di categoria**. Il pattern Akeneo-style
    è realizzato dall'entità autonoma `ProductType`, non da una proprietà
    di un nodo categoria-radice (deviazione consapevole dal design
    originale, documentata in [riepilogo-design.md](./riepilogo-design.md)
    sezioni 3.4-3.6).

- [x] **9b. UI Catalogo (Miller columns) nel core.** Modulo `Catalog/` con
  `Level` value object + `CatalogHierarchy` registry (singleton) + Filament
  Page `Catalog` con view Blade Livewire. Layout colonne side-by-side,
  drill-down via `selectRecord(depth, id)`, breadcrumb cliccabile, link
  "Apri" verso la Resource del livello. Il template configura la catena
  in `AppServiceProvider::defineCatalogHierarchy()` (Category1 → Category2
  → Product). Sub-entità del Product previste dal contratto (`Level::childLevelsFor`
  ritorna lista ordinata di Level + UI tab switcher quando N > 1) ma
  vuote in v1 — entreranno in gioco al task #22b.
  - Catena dichiarata sul template: il core resta agnostic sui modelli
    del cliente.
  - Le tre Resource esistenti (Category1/2, Product) restano: la Page
    Catalogo le orchestra, non le sostituisce.
  - `Level` espone anche `childrenQuery`, `cardLabel`, `cardSubtitle` come
    closure opzionali, oltre a `pluralLabel()`/`singularLabel()` risolti
    dal file lang `{model_snake}.model[_plural]`.

- [x] **10. Trait `HasAssets` nel core.** Wrap su `HasMedia` di spatie
  (senza folder support per ora), config media-library, applicazione su
  `Product` nel template.
  - **Planning lockato (giugno 2026, design §4.11)**: #10/#15/#16 sono una
    sola linea di lavoro sequenziale. Modulo nuovo `src/Assets/` (namespace
    `AtrioTeam\DigitalHub\Assets\`). Migrazioni asset owned dal core via
    `loadMigrationsFrom` (pattern nuovo: oggi il SP non carica migrazioni).
    Valutati e scartati 4 package Filament (vedi §4.11): build custom con

    public static function make(array | Closure $actions): static
    {

    public function isHidden(): bool
    {
        if (parent::isHidden()) {
            return true;
        }

                return false;
            }
        }

        return $this;

    public function isFullWidth(): bool
    {
        return (bool) $this->evaluate($this->isFullWidth);
    }

    /**

    public function beforeLabel(array | Schema | Component | Action | ActionGroup | string | Htmlable | Closure | null $components): static

        return $this;

# Example: Browser-driven web app

You have a dev server that serves HTML to a browser. An agent in a
headless container can't open a browser window — so "run the app" means
launching the dev server, driving a headless Chromium against it, and
producing a screenshot that proves the page rendered.

Don't write a browser driver. Use `chromium-cli`.

## Dev server

Find the dev command (`package.json` `scripts.dev`, `Makefile`,
README), start it in the background, and wait for it to actually serve:

```bash
npm run dev &   # or yarn dev, pnpm dev, make serve, ./dev.sh
echo $! > /tmp/dev.pid
timeout 30 bash -c 'until curl -sf http://localhost:3000 >/dev/null; do sleep 1; done'
```

Don't `sleep 5` — poll the port. Stop with
`kill $(cat /tmp/dev.pid)` (or `pkill -f 'npm run dev'`) before
relaunching, or the next run hits `EADDRINUSE`.

## Drive

`chromium-cli` is a headless-Chromium REPL. Pipe a script to stdin:

```bash
chromium-cli --session app <<'EOF'
nav http://localhost:3000
wait-for text=Dashboard
screenshot
click button:has-text("New item")
fill input[name="title"] Smoke test
press Enter
wait-for text=Smoke test
screenshot
console --errors
EOF
```

Screenshots land in `chromium_cli/sessions/app/screenshots/` (latest
symlinked as `screenshot.png`). That's the whole loop: `nav` →
`wait-for` the element you need → act (`click` / `fill` / `type` /
`press`) → `screenshot` → `console --errors` to check nothing threw.
Full command reference: `chromium-cli` skill, or `help` at the prompt.

For iterative debugging, run it under tmux and `send-keys` one command
at a time — same commands, same session.

**If `chromium-cli` isn't available:** adapt
[electron.md](electron.md)'s REPL driver — the structure and commands
transfer, but it's `_electron`-specific:
import `{ chromium }` instead, launch with
`chromium.launch({ args: ['--no-sandbox'] })`, acquire the page via
`(await app.newContext()).newPage()` then `goto()` your dev URL, and
drop the Electron-only window introspection
(`.windows()`/`.firstWindow()`/the `windows` command).

## What to put in the skill

The project-specific bits only. `chromium-cli` handles the mechanics.

- **Dev command + port + stop.** The exact start line, any env vars it
  needs, and the `kill`/`pkill` to stop it.
- **Auth.** Whatever gets a logged-in session — a `set-cookie` line, a
  `fill`/`click` login sequence, or a helper script that does the API
  dance and emits the cookie.
- **One representative interaction.** Not the whole app — one path that
  proves it's running, ending in a screenshot.
- **App-specific gotchas.** Only the ones you actually hit.

## Gotchas that recur

- **React controlled inputs.** `eval el.value = '…'` doesn't fire
  React's onChange. Use `fill` / `type` — they go through Playwright's
  input pipeline.
- **Websockets / long-poll.** `wait-idle` never settles. `wait-for` the
  element you actually need.
- **Slow first paint.** Vite/Next compile routes on demand; the first
  `nav` can take 10s+. `wait-for` handles it; raw `sleep` doesn't.
- **`screenshot-element <sel>`** crops to one element — use it when the
  diff is in a specific component, not the whole page.
- **Check `console --errors` before declaring success.** A page can
  render its shell while every data fetch 500s.

    public function test_info_panel_mounts_without_errors_for_processed_image(): void
    {
        Storage::fake('assets');

        $this->actingAs(User::factory()->create());
        Filament::setCurrentPanel('admin');

        $product = Product::create(['name' => ['it' => 'Tavolo']]);
        $media = $product
            ->addMediaFromString($this->jpeg(40, 25))
            ->usingFileName('photo.jpg')
            ->toMediaCollection('assets');

        $this->artisan('digital-hub:extract-metadata')->assertSuccessful();

        // mountAction + render valutano la closure dello schema (tab + sezioni +

        Livewire::test(AssetManager::class, ['ownerType' => 'product', 'owner' => $product->getKey()])
            ->mountAction('infoAsset', ['media' => $media->getKey()])
            ->assertActionMounted('infoAsset')
            ->assertOk();
    }

    private function jpeg(int $width, int $height): string
    {
        $image = imagecreatetruecolor($width, $height);
        ob_start();
        imagejpeg($image);

        return (string) ob_get_clean();
    }
}

use AtrioTeam\DigitalHub\Assets\Filament\Pages\AssetManager;
use AtrioTeam\DigitalHub\Assets\Jobs\ProcessAssetJob;
use AtrioTeam\DigitalHub\Assets\Metadata\ExtractedMetadata;
use AtrioTeam\DigitalHub\Assets\Models\Media as TaggableMedia;
use AtrioTeam\DigitalHub\Assets\Support\AssetDuplicator;
use AtrioTeam\DigitalHub\Assets\Support\AssetPreview;
use AtrioTeam\DigitalHub\Assets\Support\AssetProcessingStatus;
use AtrioTeam\DigitalHub\Tags\Models\Tag;
use Filament\Facades\Filament;
use Illuminate\Foundation\Testing\RefreshDatabase;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Queue;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Storage;
use Livewire\Livewire;
use Tests\TestCase;

/**
 * Duplicazione di un asset (digital-hub 14e): nuovo record Media con copia
 * fisica del file (stessi owner/disco/collection/folder), suffisso "(copia N)"
 * su `name` e (sanitizzato) su `file_name`, tag replicati; metadati/anteprima
 * non copiati — la copia riparte `pending` col job di rielaborazione in coda.
 */
class AssetDuplicateTest extends TestCase
{
    use RefreshDatabase;

    public function test_duplicate_creates_new_record_with_copied_file_and_requeues_processing(): void
    {
        Storage::fake('assets');
        Queue::fake();

        $user = User::factory()->create();
        $this->actingAs($user);

        $product = Product::create(['name' => ['it' => 'Tavolo']]);
        $folder = $product->createAssetFolder('Schede');
        $media = $product
            ->addMediaFromString('contenuto originale')
            ->usingName('Scheda tecnica')
            ->usingFileName('scheda.txt')
            ->toMediaCollection('assets');
        $media->setAttribute('asset_folder_id', $folder->getKey());

        // simula un asset già elaborato: metadati estratti + poster generato
        ExtractedMetadata::write($media, ['common' => ['size' => 19]]);
        $disk = Storage::disk('assets');
        $disk->put(AssetPreview::relativePath($media), 'poster');
        $media->setCustomProperty(AssetPreview::PROPERTY, AssetPreview::relativePath($media));
        $media->setAttribute('processing_status', AssetProcessingStatus::Completed->value);
        $media->save();

        $copy = AssetDuplicator::duplicate($media);

        // nuovo record: stesso owner/collection/folder; suffisso su name e
        // (sanitizzato, spazi → trattini) su file_name
        $this->assertNotSame($media->getKey(), $copy->getKey());
        $this->assertSame($media->model_type, $copy->model_type);
        $this->assertSame($media->model_id, $copy->model_id);
        $this->assertSame('assets', $copy->collection_name);
        $this->assertSame($folder->getKey(), $copy->getAttribute('asset_folder_id'));
        $this->assertSame('scheda-(copia).txt', $copy->file_name);
        $this->assertSame('Scheda tecnica (copia)', $copy->name);

        // copia fisica: entrambi i file esistono, contenuto identico
        $disk->assertExists($media->getPathRelativeToRoot());
        $disk->assertExists($copy->getPathRelativeToRoot());
        $this->assertSame('contenuto originale', $disk->get($copy->getPathRelativeToRoot()));

        // uploader = chi duplica; derivati non copiati, rielaborazione in coda
        $this->assertSame($user->getKey(), $copy->getAttribute('uploaded_by_id'));
        $this->assertSame([], ExtractedMetadata::forMedia($copy));
        $this->assertNull($copy->getCustomProperty(AssetPreview::PROPERTY));
        $this->assertSame(AssetProcessingStatus::Pending->value, $copy->getAttribute('processing_status'));
        Queue::assertPushed(ProcessAssetJob::class, fn (ProcessAssetJob $job): bool => $job->mediaId === $copy->getKey());

        // l'originale resta intatto
        $media->refresh();
        $this->assertSame('Scheda tecnica', $media->name);
        $this->assertSame(AssetProcessingStatus::Completed->value, $media->getAttribute('processing_status'));
    }

    public function test_copy_suffix_is_progressive_and_not_stacked(): void
    {
        Storage::fake('assets');
        Queue::fake();

        $product = Product::create(['name' => ['it' => 'Tavolo']]);
        $media = $product
            ->addMediaFromString('contenuto')
            ->usingName('Doc')
            ->usingFileName('doc.txt')
            ->toMediaCollection('assets');

        $first = AssetDuplicator::duplicate($media);
        $second = AssetDuplicator::duplicate($media);
        // duplicare una copia non accumula suffissi: "Doc (copia) (copia)" mai
        $third = AssetDuplicator::duplicate($first);

        $this->assertSame('Doc (copia)', $first->name);
        $this->assertSame('Doc (copia 2)', $second->name);
        $this->assertSame('Doc (copia 3)', $third->name);

        // stesso suffisso, sanitizzato, sul file_name (senza accumulo)
        $this->assertSame('doc-(copia).txt', $first->file_name);
        $this->assertSame('doc-(copia-2).txt', $second->file_name);
        $this->assertSame('doc-(copia-3).txt', $third->file_name);
    }

    public function test_suffix_is_scoped_to_the_folder_of_the_original(): void
    {
        Storage::fake('assets');
        Queue::fake();

        $product = Product::create(['name' => ['it' => 'Tavolo']]);
        $folder = $product->createAssetFolder('Schede');

        // in root esiste già "Doc (copia)"; l'originale sta in una folder,
        // dove quel nome è libero
        $product->addMediaFromString('x')->usingName('Doc (copia)')->usingFileName('a.txt')->toMediaCollection('assets');
        $media = $product->addMediaFromString('y')->usingName('Doc')->usingFileName('b.txt')->toMediaCollection('assets');
        $media->setAttribute('asset_folder_id', $folder->getKey());
        $media->save();

        $copy = AssetDuplicator::duplicate($media);

        $this->assertSame('Doc (copia)', $copy->name);
        $this->assertSame($folder->getKey(), $copy->getAttribute('asset_folder_id'));
    }

    public function test_duplicate_copies_tags(): void
    {
        Storage::fake('assets');
        Queue::fake();

        $product = Product::create(['name' => ['it' => 'Tavolo']]);
        $media = $product
            ->addMediaFromString('contenuto')
            ->usingName('Doc')
            ->usingFileName('doc.txt')
            ->toMediaCollection('assets');

        $tag = Tag::create(['name' => 'Rosso']);
        $this->assertInstanceOf(TaggableMedia::class, $media);
        $media->tags()->sync([$tag->getKey()]);

        $copy = AssetDuplicator::duplicate($media);

        $this->assertInstanceOf(TaggableMedia::class, $copy);
        $this->assertSame([$tag->getKey()], $copy->tags()->pluck('tags.id')->all());
    }

    public function test_duplicate_action_is_wired_in_asset_manager(): void
    {
        Storage::fake('assets');
        Queue::fake();

        $this->actingAs(User::factory()->create());
        Filament::setCurrentPanel('admin');

        $product = Product::create(['name' => ['it' => 'Tavolo']]);
        $media = $product
            ->addMediaFromString('contenuto')
            ->usingName('Doc')
            ->usingFileName('doc.txt')
            ->toMediaCollection('assets');

        Livewire::test(AssetManager::class, ['ownerType' => 'product', 'owner' => $product->getKey()])
            ->callAction('duplicateAsset', arguments: ['media' => $media->getKey()])
            ->assertHasNoActionErrors()
            ->assertOk();

        $this->assertSame(2, $product->media()->where('collection_name', 'assets')->count());
        $this->assertNotNull($product->media()->where('name', 'Doc (copia)')->first());
    }
}

class AssetInfoPanelTest extends TestCase
{
    use RefreshDatabase;

    public function test_info_panel_mounts_without_errors_for_processed_image(): void
    {
        Storage::fake('assets');

        $this->actingAs(User::factory()->create());
        Filament::setCurrentPanel('admin');

        $product = Product::create(['name' => ['it' => 'Tavolo']]);
        $media = $product
            ->addMediaFromString($this->jpeg(40, 25))
            ->usingFileName('photo.jpg')
            ->toMediaCollection('assets');

        $this->artisan('digital-hub:extract-metadata')->assertSuccessful();

        // mountAction + render valutano la closure dello schema (tab + sezioni +
        // KeyValueEntry): se la composizione fosse malformata, qui lancerebbe.
        Livewire::test(AssetManager::class, ['ownerType' => 'product', 'owner' => $product->getKey()])
            ->mountAction('infoAsset', ['media' => $media->getKey()])
            ->assertActionMounted('infoAsset')
            ->assertOk();
    }

    /**
     * 14e: lo slideover info espone duplica/condividi/scarica/elimina, riuso
     * delle stesse action del menu contestuale con `media` già in argument.
     */
    public function test_info_panel_exposes_duplicate_share_download_delete_actions(): void
    {
        Storage::fake('assets');

        $this->actingAs(User::factory()->create());
        Filament::setCurrentPanel('admin');

        $product = Product::create(['name' => ['it' => 'Tavolo']]);
        $media = $product
            ->addMediaFromString($this->jpeg(40, 25))
            ->usingFileName('photo.jpg')
            ->toMediaCollection('assets');

        Livewire::test(AssetManager::class, ['ownerType' => 'product', 'owner' => $product->getKey()])
            ->mountAction('infoAsset', ['media' => $media->getKey()])
            ->assertSeeHtml('wire:click="mountAction(\'duplicateAsset\'')
            ->assertSeeHtml('wire:click="mountAction(\'shareAsset\'')
            ->assertSeeHtml('wire:click="mountAction(\'downloadAsset\'')
            ->assertSeeHtml('wire:click="mountAction(\'deleteAsset\'');
    }

    private function jpeg(int $width, int $height): string
    {
        $image = imagecreatetruecolor($width, $height);
        ob_start();
        imagejpeg($image);

        return (string) ob_get_clean();
    }
}

<?php

namespace Filament\Support\View\Components;

use Filament\Support\Colors\Color;
use Filament\Support\Facades\FilamentColor;
use Filament\Support\View\Components\ColorMaps\ButtonComponentColorMap;
use Filament\Support\View\Components\ColorMaps\ComponentColorMap;
use Filament\Support\View\Components\Contracts\HasColor;
use Filament\Support\View\Components\Contracts\HasDefaultGrayColor;

class ButtonComponent implements HasColor, HasDefaultGrayColor
{
    public function __construct(
        public readonly bool $isOutlined = false,
    ) {}

    /**
     * @param  array<int, string>  $color
     * @return array<string, int>
     */
    public function getColorMap(array $color): array
    {
        $gray = FilamentColor::getColor('gray');

        if ($this->isOutlined) {
            return ComponentColorMap::make($color)
                ->slot('text', surface: $gray[50], minRatio: Color::WCAG_AA_TEXT, fallback: 900)
                ->slot('dark:text', surface: $gray[700], minRatio: Color::WCAG_AA_TEXT, maxShade: 500, shouldStartFromDarkest: true, fallback: 200)
                ->get();
        }

        return ButtonComponentColorMap::make($color)
            ->minContrastRatio(Color::WCAG_AA_TEXT)
            ->lightBackground(bg: 600, hover: 500)
            ->lightBackground(bg: 400, hover: 300, alternateHover: 500)
            ->darkBackground(bg: 600, hover: 500, alternateHover: 700)
            ->get();
    }
}
